Package hadur117.core.move

Class ReplicatorWeights

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.move.ReplicatorWeights
final class ReplicatorWeights extends Object
MOVE-16: the per-battle multipliers that let the danger views reproduce in proportion to how well each predicted the bullets that actually came (the discrete replicator equation). A view's effective weight in the danger average is its fixed weight times its multiplier; every multiplier starts at 1.

When an enemy bullet's true angle becomes known, each view that is on rates it with a probability density d_i over the guess factors in [-1, 1] (see density(double, double[])), mixed with a little uniform density so a view that missed entirely is not wiped out: p_i = (1 - EPSILON) d_i + EPSILON / 2. Then m_i <- m_i p_i / pbar, where pbar = sum_j w_j m_j p_j / sum_j w_j m_j is the effective-weight average of the predictions, so a view that beat the average gains share and one that fell short loses it. Afterwards no on-view's share of the on-views' effective weight stays below FLOOR (mutation: a view can come back when the enemy changes gun), and no multiplier exceeds MAX.

Only the views that are on take part; the others keep their multipliers. The class holds numbers only, so it knows nothing of the views, waves or the switch.
